title: CU-01 Windows CUA spike result
description: Evidence contract for reports/computer/spikes/<runid>/result.json. AUTHORED 2026-10-23, NOT YET PRODUCED BY A RUN — every field is a claim about where a value comes from, derived from pinned OpenClaw 013240515205573248c27ab6b8eec7303f0da1a8 plus zero-policy v0.1.3, and is [needs GO] until a live run fills it. OpenCode's five CU-01 asks are folded in; the two that the desktop relay cannot supply are declared `unavailableFromRelay` rather than quietly dropped. DeepSeek's two G-G captures are refusalObserved and inputKind/codeModePathUnreachableUnderD011. `holdRecovery` (G-G item 15) records the no-pagehide disconnect path separately because it cannot be inferred from a normal release.

runId.description: Synthetic id, e.g. cu01-2026-10-23-a. Never a machine name.

operatorRoleLabel.description: Role label only. Never a Windows account name.

zeroPolicyVersion.description: zero-policy plugin version. 0.1.3 is the first release whose hold is bound to the owning connection's abort signal; k7 is not attributable to an older version.

doctorDriverArtifacts.description: Gate G-C pass condition is `no findings`.

environment.description: Copied from computer/spike/preflight.ps1 output, with the account name redacted.

sessionKind.description: CU-00 4.5: the node must start inside the interactive desktop session. This field is how a later COMPUTER_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE is explained.

primaryResolution.description: WxH of the delivered screenshot, not the physical panel.

scalingPercent.description: Non-100 is expected to throw COMPUTER_UNSUPPORTED_DISPLAY on non-macOS (commands.ts:498-506).

baseline.description: The advertised provider surface, read BEFORE any action, compared against computer/contracts/computer-act-actions.json.

nodeId.description: Opaque node reference; not a hostname.

missingVsDerived.description: Must be empty, else upstream drifted and the taxonomy doc needs regenerating.

steps.description: S1..S11 from reports/computer/cu01-spike-protocol.md. S11 is EXPECTED to fail on unmodified upstream (takeover gap) — recording that failure is the deliverable, not a defect to hide.

action.description: The computer/computer.act action name actually sent, from the derived taxonomy.

command.description: Routing proof: screenshot/wait ride screen.snapshot; every other action including structured observation rides computer.act (computer-tool-request.ts:20-23).

request.description: Synthetic arguments only. Strip absolute paths and real account data.

effect.description: Provider effect evidence. `applied` is NOT proof the app responded (computer-use.md:130) - that is what step S6 proves.

frame.description: Model-side observation identity. Exists only on the screen.snapshot / get_window_state paths.

capturedAtUtc.description: SPIKE-LOCAL timestamp. Upstream snapshot results do NOT carry a capture timestamp; the rig stamps receive time. Declared so nobody reads it as provider-produced.

unchangedFromPrevious.description: Upstream returns metadata-only when the screen is pixel-identical (computer-use.md:102); the frameId then stays valid.

holder.description: OpenCode ask 2 + 4. Control-holder state at this step. The authoritative source is the D-009 zero.computer.control snapshot, NOT the relay.

controlLeaseId.description: Opaque, server-minted. Present only when owned===true (verified backend/plugin/index.js:349); a status poll by a non-holding client legitimately omits it, so absence is not a failure.

resumeSnapshotRequired.description: True after a human release. Freshness clears only on a desktop capture: screenshot, wait, or get_window_state WITH includeScreenshot=true — a window observation without an image does not prove the desktop underneath is unchanged.

inputRefusedWithReason.description: Expect computer-hold:human-control while held; zero-policy:unknown-action fails closed; computer-hold:stale-frame after release until a fresh screenshot.

scope.description: Mirrors the plugin snapshot (backend/plugin/index.js:346). Load-bearing, not an ignorable extra: it is the only signal that the hold is not per-target (C7). A panel must not imply per-conversation ownership from it.

recentCount.description: Length of the plugin bounded recent-decision ring in the snapshot; evidence that a refusal was recorded for audit, not just returned.

liveView.description: OpenCode ask 1 + 3, and the honest limit: the desktop relay is raw RFB over a dedicated binary WebSocket (config-browser-ui-desktop.md:406-408) and its client surface exposes only connect/disconnect/securityFailure + input methods (ui/src/components/desktop/desktop-client.ts:28-60). There is NO frameId, NO sequence, NO capturedAt and NO per-frame geometry event on the relay path. Staleness on the panel MUST be derived from local receive/paint time, never claimed as provider metadata.

closeCode.description: 1006 alone does not identify a network failure (computer-use.md:342).

secondsSinceLastPaint.description: SPIKE-LOCAL derivation. This is the only staleness signal the MVP can honestly produce for the human view.

humanInputReachedDesktop.description: Measured at S11: whether interactive RFB input and agent foreground input collide, and in what order effects landed.

unavailableFromRelay.description: Declared-missing, not silently omitted. Anything a consumer wants here needs a separate, explicit mechanism.

hostSideVerification.description: S6. The only step that can prove the task happened. A screenshot never counts.

approved.description: file.* and system.run need their own pairing/approval; exec host=node is a separate opt-in.

sentinelMatched.description: Decoded content equals the synthetic sentinel.

stop.description: S9. Two deliberately different layers: agent-side refusal vs gateway command denial.

inFlightNativeActionStopped.description: Expected FALSE for a tool-layer hold (it gates new calls); run interrupt is what cancels in-flight via SDK (computer-use.md:242,303). Record, do not fix.

screenshotStillWorkedAfterDeny.description: Expected TRUE: screenshot rides screen.snapshot, so the global stop degrades observation rather than blinding it.

evidenceFiles.description: Relative names inside the run folder. Synthetic fixture content only; discard anything that caught personal data.

refusalObserved.description: DeepSeek G-G capture (a): the refusal EXACTLY as the model receives it, not what the plugin returned internally. If the host re-wraps it, OpenCode cannot render the hold reason and DeepSeek audit keys mismatch. Record raw text and structured fields separately.

rawToolResultText.description: Verbatim tool-result text returned to the model.

reasonAsSeenByModel.description: Expected: computer-hold:human-control verbatim. Record any host-added wrapping.

degradedToGenericPolicyFailure.description: True if it arrived as `blocked by zero-policy.computer-hold: policy evaluation failed` or similar instead of our code — that means the Operator cannot explain the hold to the user.

surfacesInSessionToolEvents.description: OpenCode dependency: does the refusal appear as a session.tool event?

inputKind.description: Matches the plugin audit field (backend/plugin/index.js:247). Under D-011 the Operator cannot reach the code-mode path at all (exec denied), so `code_mode_exec` rows appear only if exec is deliberately re-enabled in the test environment.

negativeChecks.description: Cheap guardrail proofs. Each is a refusal, not a failure.

holdRecovery.description: G-G item 15 / CU-02: connection death without pagehide. The core claim (the hold is freed and the fresh-capture gate is armed) was proven live at the Gateway layer on 2026-10-23 08:34 IST with zero-policy 0.1.3; this block records the re-proof on the designated environment, where the agent-side stale-frame half can also be exercised. A normal release button is NOT this check: if pagehide ran, set ownerConnectionClosedWithoutPagehide=false and k7 cannot pass.

ownerConnectionClosedWithoutPagehide.description: True only if the holding connection died without running its pagehide handler: renderer/tab kill, network loss, or a raw WS close. Say which one in `note`. A clicked Release, or a pagehide that ran, does not count.

ownerConnectionPath.description: How the owner connection was held and killed. `cli` is the k7-run one-shot process close; `raw-ws` is a long-lived socket destroyed without close; `control-ui` is the real panel/tab kill. The host abort path is the same, but the run must say which one it actually did.

statusReadFromNewConnection.description: The status below was read on a connection created after the owner died, not on the dead or a pre-existing connection.

resumeSnapshotRequiredBefore.description: Expected false. H3's true is attributable to this disconnect only if the gate was clear before the take; if it is true, capture a fresh frame first. Null only when the run was refused or the before-status was unreadable.

held.description: Expected false: the dead owner's hold must be gone, not merely unowned.

owned.description: Expected false: a new connection never inherits the lease.

resumeSnapshotRequired.description: Expected true: the same gate a normal hand-back arms.

releasedByDisconnectBefore.description: stats.releasedByDisconnect read immediately before the owner connection is killed.

releasedByDisconnectAfter.description: Expected before + 1. This is what attributes the release to the disconnect rather than to an earlier hand-back.

action.description: Synthetic input action, e.g. left_click or type.

refused.description: True if the tool layer refused the input.

desktopEffect.description: Observed desktop effect of the refused input. k7 requires `none`; `landed` means the refusal did not prevent the action and is a bug, not a pass.

freshCaptureClearedGate.description: After a screenshot (or wait), the same input action is no longer stale-frame refused. A window observation without includeScreenshot:true does not clear it.

note.description: How the owner connection was killed, and any host-side error code. Synthetic text only.

k1.description: Provider registered on Windows with the expected surface.

k3.description: Human watched the run through the relay.

k4.description: A global stop worked without a restart.

k5.description: Takeover arbitration. Expected FALSE on unmodified upstream; the recorded refusal IS the CU-03 evidence.

k6.description: Recovery revoked refs and did not replay the interrupted action.

k7.description: G-G item 15: the owning connection died WITHOUT pagehide, a new connection saw held:false / resumeSnapshotRequired:true, releasedByDisconnect incremented, a connection-closed lease row exists, agent input was stale-frame refused, and a fresh capture cleared the gate. A normal release cannot satisfy this.

takeoverGapConfirmed.description: S11 result: upstream throws `take_control is only available for an attached or session desktop` for gateway/node targets. Expected true.

backgroundDeliveryOutcome.description: Assumption A5. If it always refuses, pixel-only driving is the norm and the custom-provider case strengthens.

notClaimed.description: Explicit list of things this run does NOT prove. Required so a green K2 is never read as production-readiness.

missingScopeVsUnavailable.description: OpenCode panel-state dependency: distinguish `missingScope` (credential/privilege refusal, e.g. desktop.observe needs operator.admin) from `unavailable` (node down or desktop absent). Rendered identically, a permission gap looks like an outage.

codeModePathUnreachableUnderD011.description: G-G item 8(a): confirm Operator exec denial removes the code-mode route to the computer entirely, so the plugin matcher is genuinely defence in depth rather than the only control.

visionPathVerified.description: G-G/G-F item 11: the selected NVIDIA NIM model actually received the delivered desktop frame and returned coordinates in that image space. Catalogue image-input claim is not evidence for this lane.
